chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man peeked at the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) from the reeds. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'If I knew that you would stand still for me, I would come to you with the arrow until I blind your eye with it.' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'Is that for us as well?' He said: 'Woe to you or suffering to you! I am telling you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did it, and you say, 'Is that for us?''

key_terms.أَفْقَأَ: To blind or put out an eye
key_terms.الْجَرِيد: Reeds or palm fronds used for screening
key_terms.الْمِشْقَص: A specific type of arrow or dart

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Prophet's threat to blind the man with an arrow in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the concept of *al-Mu'ta'ah* (the one for whom there is no wergild), illustrating the unique, absolute authority of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) compared to the Imams. When asked if the Prophet's severe reaction to being watched applied to the Imams, the Imam clarified that the Prophet's action was specific to his prophetic status, distinguishing his divine prerogative from the Imams' derived authority. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle that while Imams possess high status, they do not share the Prophet's exclusive *mu'tah* status regarding blood money exemptions.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘A man peeked at the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> from the reeds, so the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘If I<sup>saww</sup> knew you would be standing still for me<sup>saww</sup>, I<sup>saww</sup> would have come to you with the arrow until I<sup>saww</sup> poke your eyes with it’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is that for us (as well)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you!’, or ‘Suffering be upon you!’ I<sup>asws</sup> am saying to you that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did it. You are saying, ‘Is that for us?’
